entries.do_not_use_when: joy without relief or satisfaction, e.g. a plain happy surprise; also not for revenge in a sad scene
entries.example_neutral: Team jeet gayi, mujhe bahut khushi hui.
entries.example_edited: Team jeet gayi, mere dil ko thandak mil gayi.

entries.do_not_use_when: joy from effort or fun; fits only sudden luck or windfalls
entries.example_neutral: Free tickets mil gaye, mujhe bahut khushi hui.
entries.example_edited: Free tickets mil gaye, mujhe toh lottery lag gayi.

entries.do_not_use_when: sad or formal moments
entries.example_neutral: Sabke saath trip pe jaana bahut maza hai.
entries.example_edited: Sabke saath trip pe jaana bahut maze ki baat hai.

entries.do_not_use_when: sad moments; a bit filmy and close in feel to 'garden-garden', so use only one of the two in a scene
entries.example_neutral: Maa ka phone aaya, mera dil khush ho gaya.
entries.example_edited: Maa ka phone aaya, mera dil baag-baag ho gaya.

entries.do_not_use_when: very casual banter, where it sounds too formal or poetic
entries.example_neutral: Mujhe tum par bahut garv hai.
entries.example_edited: Mujhe tum par bahut fakhr hai.

entries.do_not_use_when: jokey or sarcastic lines, since it is warm and heartfelt
entries.example_neutral: Mujhe apne dost par bahut garv hai.
entries.example_edited: Mujhe apne dost par bahut naaz hai.

entries.do_not_use_when: loud celebration moments, since it is soft and sincere
entries.example_neutral: Mujhe tum par bahut garv hai.
entries.example_edited: Mujhe tum par bahut maan hai.

entries.do_not_use_when: serious or solemn moments, or when you want to sound humble
entries.example_neutral: Tumhara result dekh kar mujhe garv hua.
entries.example_edited: Tumhara result dekh kar meri chhaati phool gayi.

entries.do_not_use_when: serious moments, or around people who may read it as a political joke
entries.example_neutral: Tumhari jeet dekh kar mujhe bahut garv hua.
entries.example_edited: Tumhari jeet dekh kar meri chhaati 56 inch ki ho gayi.

entries.do_not_use_when: casual or jokey lines, since it sounds a bit filmy and family-honour-ish
entries.example_neutral: Tumhari wajah se mujhe garv hai.
entries.example_edited: Tumhari wajah se mera sar ooncha ho gaya.

entries.do_not_use_when: serious or sad moments, talking to elders
entries.example_neutral: Uski baatein sunke mera gussa chadh gaya.
entries.example_edited: Uski baatein sunke mera pitta chadh gaya.

entries.do_not_use_when: serious or sad moments, talking to elders
entries.example_neutral: Traffic mein phanse-phanse mera gussa chadh gaya.
entries.example_edited: Traffic mein phanse-phanse mera paara chadh gaya.

entries.do_not_use_when: calm or formal talk, describing yourself as mildly annoyed
entries.example_neutral: Result dekhte hi wo mujh par gussa ho gaya.
entries.example_edited: Result dekhte hi wo mujh par aag-babula ho gaya.

entries.do_not_use_when: light-hearted irritation, since it suggests violent rage
entries.example_neutral: Aaj uske sar pe gussa sawar hai.
entries.example_edited: Aaj uske sar pe khoon sawar hai.

entries.do_not_use_when: only for looks, outfits, pairings or vibes; not for songs, food or ideas
entries.example_neutral: Mujhe yeh jacket bahut pasand hai.
entries.example_edited: Mujhe yeh jacket bahut jam raha hai.
